financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis. EPS 0.55 = 1,219m/2,209,867,246 confirmed. See GROUP row's notes for shared extraction/verification detail.

People's Leasing & Finance PLC (PLC), licensed finance company, subsidiary of People's Bank. IMPORTANT EXTRACTION NOTE: several GROUP subtotal rows in this filing's P&L (Net interest income, Total operating income, Net operating income, Profit for the period) were printed with the two comparative periods in the OPPOSITE order to the surrounding rows -- a genuine dual-column artifact seen elsewhere this session (e.g. TILE, PARQ's segmental table). Resolved via bottom-up arithmetic: every individual line item (interest income, interest expense, fee income, premiums, impairment, personnel/admin expenses, tax on financial services, income tax) was independently verified against its own printed % change (which uniquely determines direction regardless of column position), then summed upward through each subtotal; every subtotal recomputed this way ties EXACTLY to the next verified figure (e.g. Operating profit before tax on financial services, Profit before tax, Profit for the period, and EPS = attributable profit/2,209,867,246 shares = 0.6024 ~= disclosed 0.60), giving high confidence in the final figures despite the printing artifact. Mapped per this project's NBFI convention: revenue = 'Total operating income' (Net interest income + net earned premiums + fee/commission income + net gains on FVTPL + other operating income); operating_profit = 'Operating profit before tax on financial services', the company's own subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- interest expense is already netted into revenue via Net interest income, so a separate line would double count. 'Tax on financial services' (Rs.848mn Group / Rs.791mn Company this quarter) is not a separate stored field -- it sits inside the bridge from operating_profit to profit_before_tax; profit_before_tax stored here is AFTER this levy, matching the filing's own 'Profit before income tax' line. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split, and 'Loans and receivables' is the core lending book, not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks'; long_term_borrowings = 'Debt securities issued'. 'Due to customers' (deposits, Rs.185,293mn Group) is deliberately excluded from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt. 'Other financial liabilities' (Rs.7,478mn Group) also excluded -- not clearly identified as interest-bearing debt in this filing. capex (Group) = 'Purchase of property, plant and equipment' (170) + 'Purchase of intangible assets' (12) = 182; capex (Company) = 63+2=65. Net cash from investing activities for both Company (943) and Group (464) required the same bottom-up reconstruction as the P&L subtotals (the printed row order for the Company column specifically was reversed for this one line).

interim_updates.note_text: People's Leasing & Finance PLC's Group Total Operating Income grew 42.9% YoY to Rs.9,503mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), driven by interest income growth of 65.3% (Rs.8,985mn to Rs.14,855mn). By segment, growth was led overwhelmingly by the Loans segment: interest income more than doubled (+109.2%, Rs.3,268mn to Rs.6,837mn) and segment assets nearly doubled (+87.9%, Rs.103,126mn to Rs.193,694mn), far outpacing the Lease & Hire Purchase segment's more moderate growth (interest income +33.0%, segment assets +24.6% to Rs.133,028mn). Funding costs grew even faster than interest income (interest expense +90.7% to Rs.7,537mn), a margin-pressure signal, but Net Interest Income still grew a healthy 45.4% (Rs.5,032mn to Rs.7,318mn) off the larger base. Impairment charges and other losses for loans and receivables jumped from just Rs.36mn to Rs.966mn (+2,583%) -- a very large swing in absolute terms, though Operating Profit before Tax on Financial Services still grew 28.5% (Rs.2,577mn to Rs.3,312mn) as income growth outpaced it. Profit for the period grew a much slower 10.7% (Rs.1,257mn to Rs.1,391mn) than PBT's 26.2% growth, because Income Tax Expense grew 54.2% (Rs.696mn to Rs.1,073mn) -- tax absorbed roughly half of the pre-tax profit increase. The standalone Company grew profit faster than the Group (PAT +28.7% to Rs.1,219mn vs Group's +10.7%), implying the Group-level growth was diluted by subsidiary-level items, including the sharply higher impairment charge (Company impairment also rose steeply, from Rs.109mn to Rs.742mn, +580.7%).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for PLC -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Note: the local document archive had also skipped the 31 March 2026 quarter (last locally-stored filing before this one was from around September 2025) -- per this project's established convention of entering only the newly-flagged period (not backfilling every gap), only this newest quarter (30 June 2026) was sourced and entered; the March 2026 gap was not backfilled.
interim_updates.takeaway: Strong headline income growth (+43% operating income) is genuinely driven by loan-book expansion (Loans segment assets +88% in a year), but two real headwinds are worth flagging: funding costs are rising faster than interest income (interest expense +91% vs interest income +65%, a margin-compression signal), and both the Group and Company booked a large step-up in impairment charges this quarter (+2,583% and +581% respectively, off small prior-year bases) -- together with a 54% jump in the tax charge, these explain why PAT growth (+10.7% Group) lagged well behind operating-income growth.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Tax on Financial Services

operational_highlights: Group Total Operating Income +42.9% YoY to Rs.9,503mn; interest income +65.3% to Rs.14,855mn
Loans segment: interest income +109.2% YoY (Rs.3,268mn to Rs.6,837mn), segment assets +87.9% (Rs.103,126mn to Rs.193,694mn) -- the dominant growth driver
Lease & Hire Purchase segment grew more moderately: interest income +33.0%, segment assets +24.6% to Rs.133,028mn
Net Interest Income +45.4% YoY to Rs.7,318mn, though interest expense (+90.7%) grew faster than interest income (+65.3%), a funding-cost/margin signal
Impairment charges and other losses for loans and receivables jumped from Rs.36mn to Rs.966mn (+2,583%) at Group level, and from Rs.109mn to Rs.742mn (+580.7%) at Company level
Group PAT grew a much slower 10.7% than the 26.2% PBT growth, as Income Tax Expense rose 54.2% (Rs.696mn to Rs.1,073mn) -- tax absorbed roughly half of the pre-tax profit gain
key_drivers: Loans segment interest income +109.2% YoY and segment assets +87.9% -- by far the largest driver of Group revenue and balance-sheet growth this quarter
Interest expense growing faster than interest income (+90.7% vs +65.3%) signals rising funding costs are compressing margin even as volumes grow strongly

A large step-up in impairment charges (+2,583% Group, +580.7% Company, both off small prior-year bases) is a genuine credit-cost increase worth monitoring, though it was still more than absorbed by income growth at the operating-profit line
Income Tax Expense growth (+54.2%) outpacing PBT growth (+26.2%) is the single biggest drag between the strong operating-profit growth and the much more modest PAT growth
